Get Volcano Plot Data

Source: R/get_volcanodata.R
get_volcanodata.Rd

Extracts and combines results from run_foldchange() and run_diff() into a single data frame. This function automatically aligns features/outcomes, retrieves fold-change and significance thresholds from the provided objects, and (optionally) keeps only "Up" or "Down" regulated features.

Usage

get_volcanodata(
  ...,
  up = NULL,
  down = NULL,
  pval = NULL,
  filter = TRUE,
  sort_es = c("desc", "asc", "none")
)

Arguments

...

Objects of class run_foldchange and/or run_diff.

up, down, pval

Optional numeric overrides for thresholds. If NULL (default), thresholds are retrieved from the objects' parameters.

filter

Logical. If TRUE (default), the data frame is filtered to include only "Up" or "Down" regulated features.

sort_es

Row order by effect size: "desc" (default) puts the largest effects first, "asc" the smallest first, and "none" keeps the original order. Features are ordered by effect size magnitude (very large, large, medium, small, very small) and then by the absolute effect size estimate. Ignored when no run_diff effect sizes are available. Note that estimates from different effect size metrics (e.g. Cohen's d vs. rank-biserial correlation) are not strictly comparable.

Value

A data.frame containing merged data from both objects: fold change columns, effect size (95\ p-value column (Adjusted p-value when present, otherwise p-value). Column names are ready for reports. When the run_diff summary table is simplified, the p-value column keeps its superscript test markers (legend stored in the "pvalue_legend" attribute and shown by as_gt). Up/Down/NS classification is used only for filter and is not returned.

Details

The function automatically detects the thresholds:

  • up and down are retrieved from the run_foldchange parameters.

  • Significance threshold (pval) is retrieved from run_diff parameters (defaulting to 0.05 if not found).

  • When run_diff result has multiple outcomes, an Adjusted p-value column is present; this function prefers it over p-value.

References

Cohen J (1988). Statistical Power Analysis for the Behavioral Sciences (2nd ed.). Lawrence Erlbaum Associates.

Benjamini Y, Hochberg Y (1995). Controlling the false discovery rate: a practical and powerful approach to multiple testing. Journal of the Royal Statistical Society: Series B, 57(1), 289-300. doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x

See also

run_foldchange, run_diff, plot_volcano, run_DIpreprocess

Author

John Lennon L. Calorio

Examples

x    <- iris[iris$Species != "setosa", 1:4]
meta <- droplevels(iris[iris$Species != "setosa", "Species", drop = FALSE])

fc  <- run_foldchange(x, metadata = meta, group = "Species")
dif <- run_diff(x, meta, outcome = names(x), group = "Species",
                summary_table = TRUE, verbose = FALSE)

get_volcanodata(fc, dif, filter = FALSE)
#>                Comparison      Feature Mean (group 1) Mean (group 2)
#> 4 versicolor vs virginica  Petal.Width          1.326          2.026
#> 3 versicolor vs virginica Petal.Length          4.260          5.552
#> 2 versicolor vs virginica Sepal.Length          5.936          6.588
#> 1 versicolor vs virginica  Sepal.Width          2.770          2.974
#>   Fold change    log2 FC          ES (95% CI)  Magnitude Adjusted p-value
#> 4   0.6544916 -0.6115534 -0.96 (-0.97, -0.94) very large           <.001ᵇ
#> 3   0.7672911 -0.3821541 -2.52 (-3.04, -1.99)      large           <.001ᵃ
#> 2   0.9010322 -0.1503495 -1.13 (-1.55, -0.70)      large           <.001ᵃ
#> 1   0.9314055 -0.1025187 -0.33 (-0.51, -0.11)      large            .005ᵇ
